# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

- **Title**: gh-1060 BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:35:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. - **PR #**: 1062
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1062
- **Title**: gh-1060 BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +100
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T19:34:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:35:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).

# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository …

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)

- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:35:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

Confirmed: the codebase explicitly documents that REST labels are `[{name}]` objects (see `prHasApproved` comment: "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"). The new `parkBlockedPr` uses `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` — with object labels this always returns -1. Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. Wait — is that wrong though? If the PR still has agent:rework and is unblocked, a rework leg would fire... The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the test mocks labels as plain strings, so the test is green while production behavior differs — a brittle/mock-shape test.

Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). The real bug is not normalizing `{name}` objects.

How does the live PR object actually reach handleReworkBlocked? Via requirePrForTicket → findPRForTicket → scm.listPrs('open') → github_list_prs → REST payload with labels as {name} objects. Unless the bridge normalizes. Let me check if there's normalization in scm.js or the bridge. Check `_githubListPrs` wrapper — in scm.js line 514, listPrs directly returns github_list_prs output. Is there any mapping? Look for where listPrs results get post-processed, e.g., in pullRequest.js or elsewhere. Let me check how mutexRegistry labelHoldersOf handles it — earlier comment in githubSource said "the github_list_prs carrier uses `number`" and prLabels(p) normalizes `(p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; })` at line 110. That's the SM path normalizing. The rework path doesn't.

Let me double-check the actual bridge global github_list_prs definition — maybe it's in native/ or a global bridge function that parses MCP output. Search for where it's defined for tests: js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js defines global.github_list_prs — check its shape to see convention.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. - **Title**: gh-1060 BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +100
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T19:34:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:35:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.

          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"

            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \

Confirmed: the codebase explicitly documents that REST labels are `[{name}]` objects (see `prHasApproved` comment: "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"). The new `parkBlockedPr` uses `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` — with object labels this always returns -1. Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. Wait — is that wrong though? If the PR still has agent:rework and is unblocked, a rework leg would fire... The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the test mocks labels as plain strings, so the test is green while production behavior differs — a brittle/mock-shape test.

Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). The real bug is not normalizing `{name}` objects.

How does the live PR object actually reach handleReworkBlocked? Via requirePrForTicket → findPRForTicket → scm.listPrs('open') → github_list_prs → REST payload with labels as {name} objects. That's the SM path normalizing. The rework path doesn't.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. - **Title**: gh-1060 BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +100
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T19:34:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:35:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.
