blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

```js
var prLabels = pr.labels || [];

```
This condition is weird: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — if labels array is empty (unknown), it does NOT skip, and calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort). blocks.text:
Root cause confirmed: `NEW > 8 js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6`. In CI, coverage matches (CI runs crap4js in $GITHUB_WORKSPACE? No — it cd's into $RUNER_TEMP/inst too... anyway, CI shows real coverage percentages). parkBlockedPr has CC=13, CRAP 14.6 > threshold 8 → new function over threshold → ratchet fails.

My local run had all N/A coverage so the ratchet couldn't flag it — a local artifact (paths). Doesn't matter; CI truth: parkBlockedPr CC 13, CRAP 14.6.

So CI failure = BLOCKING per instructions. The fix would be to split parkBlockedPr into smaller functions or add tests covering the branches to lower CRAP. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)² + CC. CC=13. For CRAP ≤ 8, need coverage: 13²(1-cov)² + 13 ≤ 8 → impossible (CRAP ≥ CC = 13 > 8). So the function must be refactored to reduce complexity below 8, or the CRAP check... Since CRAP ≥ CC always, parkBlockedPr with CC 13 can never pass threshold 8. Must refactor: split into helpers (e.g., `stripArmFromPr`, `stripArmFromIssue` — each small), reducing each function's complexity.

Now the second major finding: the label-shape bug. Let me verify what `github_list_prs` returns — REST list PRs returns labels as objects. Check ghHelpers.findPRForTicket and how other code handles labels from scm.listPrs. Let me look for existing patterns of reading pr.labels from listPrs in the codebase.
CI root cause confirmed: `NEW > 8 js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6`. Now let me verify the label-shape concern — what `scm.listPrs()` labels look like in production.

{"command":"grep -rn \"l\\.name || l\\|\\.name) || l\\|labels.*name\" js/common/pullRequest.js js/common/githubHelpers.js 2>/dev/null | head; echo ===; grep -rn \"pr.labels\\|\\.labels || \\[\\]\" js/pushReworkChanges.js | head; echo ===; grep -rn \"listPrs(\" js/common/pullRequest.js js/common/githubHelpers.js | head"}
{"command":"sed -n '120,145p' js/pushReworkChanges.js; echo ===; sed -n '1505,1530p' js/pushReworkChanges.js; echo ===; sed -n '185,200p' js/common/pullRequest.js"}

Confirmed: the codebase explicitly documents that REST labels are `[{name}]` objects (see `prHasApproved` comment: "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"). The new `parkBlockedPr` uses `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` — with object labels this always returns -1. Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. Wait — is that wrong though? If the PR still has agent:rework and is unblocked, a rework leg would fire... The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the test mocks labels as plain strings, so the test is green while production behavior differs — a brittle/mock-shape test.

Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). The real bug is not normalizing `{name}` objects.

How does the live PR object actually reach handleReworkBlocked? Via requirePrForTicket → findPRForTicket → scm.listPrs('open') → github_list_prs → REST payload with labels as {name} objects. Unless the bridge normalizes. Let me check if there's normalization in scm.js or the bridge. Check `_githubListPrs` wrapper — in scm.js line 514, listPrs directly returns github_list_prs output. Is there any mapping? Look for where listPrs results get post-processed, e.g., in pullRequest.js or elsewhere. Let me check how mutexRegistry labelHoldersOf handles it — earlier comment in githubSource said "the github_list_prs carrier uses `number`" and prLabels(p) normalizes `(p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; })` at line 110. That's the SM path normalizing. The rework path doesn't.

Let me double-check the actual bridge global github_list_prs definition — maybe it's in native/ or a global bridge function that parses MCP output. Search for where it's defined for tests: js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js defines global.github_list_prs — check its shape to see convention.
{"command":"sed -n '55,80p' js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js; echo ===; grep -rn \"labels\" js/sm/sources/githubSource.js | sed -n '1,12p'; sed -n '100,115p' js/sm/sources/githubSource.js"}

Confirmed. The SM layer (`githubSource.prLabels`) explicitly normalizes `{name}` objects → strings for exactly this reason. The rework path receives the raw REST payload where `pr.labels` is `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]`.

So `parkBlockedPr`'s guard:
```js
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```
With production data: prLabels = [{name:'agent:rework'}], indexOf('agent:rework') = -1, length = 1 > 0 → return → skip removal. Both arms skipped. PR never stripped.

Also note: `handleReworkBlocked` is called with `pr` from `requirePrForTicket` (raw listPrs object). But wait — is there a path where labels are normalized before? Let me check `ghHelpers.findPRForTicket` — the pr-N pseudo-key path uses getPr via get-by-number. Check js/common/githubHelpers.js findPRForTicket.
{"command":"sed -n '160,240p' js/common/githubHelpers.js"}

Confirmed — raw PR objects from `listPrs` are passed through; `pr.labels` in production GitHub REST payloads is `[{name: ...}]`. The new code's `indexOf(arm)` fails, and the early-return guard prevents stripping. This is a genuine production bug (partial AC failure, silent) → BLOCKING? Let's classify: the primary AC "strips arms from both the PR and the issue" fails for the PR in production. The `blocked` label addition works, which does stop the loop (the freeze is what stops re-dispatch). But on human unblock, the stale `agent:rework` arm on the PR... does any rule dispatch rework from PR-side arm without issue status? PR-side rules (pr-rework etc.) match queries with issue carriers; the issue is at status:Blocked. The SM pr-type rules read PR labels + linked issue. If a human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR while the issue stays at status:Blocked, does the rework rule fire? The rework rule presumably requires the issue NOT in blocked status... unclear. Regardless, AC explicitly requires the strip on both carriers, the PR description claims it works, and the test gives false confidence. I'd class this BLOCKING? It's a correctness bug in the new feature against the ticket AC — yes, correctness/bug → BLOCKING. But there's already one BLOCKING (CI failure). Both go in.

Wait, actually also check `handleReworkBlocked`'s own complexity: it was modified — but CI only flagged parkBlockedPr (handleReworkBlocked presumably already in baseline).

Also check: does `pr.number != null` — GitHub REST uses `number` — fine.

Another point: the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — when pr.labels is missing entirely (undefined → []), length 0 → proceeds to removeLabel best-effort. OK-ish.

Second issue: the test mocks `listPrs` returning labels as plain strings `['agent:rework','agent:review']` — doesn't match production `{name}` shape. Same class of issue.

Third: CI failure — CRAP 14.6 > 8 for new function, CC=13. CRAP ≥ CC, so must split the function. BLOCKING (red CI per formatting rules F7).

Fourth (SUGESTION/IMPORTANT): `console.log`/`console.warn` noise? Consistent with codebase style (lots of emoji logging). Fine.

Fifth: the gh-1060 test — asserts on the exact ordering of prLabelsRemoved deepEqual — fine.

Sixth: `ARMS` array — also consider `agent:dev` arm? The PR description says dev leg has no PR at blocked time. OK.

Seventh: comment-only docblock is huge (17 lines) — SUGESTION, consistent with file style though (the file has similar verbose comments).

Eighth: in the guard, when removeLabel is skipped due to "absent", fine; but with the shape bug, skipping is exactly the wrong behavior. The fix: normalize labels like `prLabels(p)` in githubSource, or simply always attempt removeLabel best-effort (like the issue-side loop does — no guard at all!). Note the asymetry: the issue-side loop has NO "absent" guard — it always calls tracker.removeLabel. Why does the PR side have the guard at all? Probably copied from somewhere. Actually, simpler and consistent: drop the guard entirely and always attempt removal (best-effort, 404 tolerated). That's what the issue side does.

Let me check where this guard pattern came from — grep for "absent — nothing to strip".

- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:35:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

- **Title**: gh-1060 BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:35:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

### Notes
- The fix relies on the existing engine-level `blocked` freeze (`matchesGuards` / `_prSideBlockedLabel` / `queryPrs` in `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`) — deliberately no SM rule/config change.
- A human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR (or moving the issue off `status:Blocked`); stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

# Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

## Summary
The fix direction is right, but two blockers: CI is red — the Quality ratchet rejects the new `parkBlockedPr` (CC 13 / CRAP 14.6 > threshold 8, and since CRAP ≥ CC no test coverage alone can bring it under) — and the PR-side arm strip silently no-ops in production because raw REST labels are `{name}` objects, so `agent:rework` stays on the PR and a human unblock would re-arm a stale rework leg (AC1 violated).

## Key Issues
- 🚨 **CI failure (Quality / crap)**: `NEW > 8 js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6` — new function over CRAP_THRESHOLD; must be split into small helpers (the file already has the gh-957 CRAP-split pattern to follow).
- 🚨 **PR arms never stripped in production**: `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` on `[{name}]` REST label objects always misses, and the `prLabels.length > 0` guard then early-returns — only the issue-side arms are actually removed.
- 💡 Test mocks PR labels as plain strings, masking the production shape; mock `{name: 'agent:rework'}` objects instead.

## Next Steps
1. Split `parkBlockedPr` into per-carrier helpers (label-block / strip-PR-arm / strip-issue-arm) so each new function stays under CC 8.
2. Normalize `pr.labels` (`l.name || l`, same as `githubSource.prLabels` / `prHasApproved`) or drop the absent-guard and best-effort `removeLabel` exactly like the issue-side loop.
3. Update the gh-1060 test to use the REST `{name}` label shape so it fails without the normalization.

`parkBlockedPr` measures CC 13. CRAP is bounded below by CC (`CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)² + CC`), so no amount of added test coverage can push a CC-13 function under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` that applies to functions not in `crap-baseline.json` — only lowering the cyclomatic complexity works.

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.

💡 **SUGGESTION: mock the production REST label shape — `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]` objects, not plain strings**

This mock is what lets the green suite mask the production bug in `parkBlockedPr` (the PR-side strip never fires against real `{name}` label objects). Please change the mock to the real REST shape:

```javascript
labels: [{ name: 'agent:rework' }, { name: 'agent:review' }]
```

That single change makes the gh-1060 test a true RED→GREEN guard for the label normalization, instead of only asserting the string-shape code path. `js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js` and the githubSource suites use the object shape for the same reason.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \

No — it cd's into $RUNER_TEMP/inst too... anyway, CI shows real coverage percentages). parkBlockedPr has CC=13, CRAP 14.6 > threshold 8 → new function over threshold → ratchet fails.

My local run had all N/A coverage so the ratchet couldn't flag it — a local artifact (paths). Doesn't matter; CI truth: parkBlockedPr CC 13, CRAP 14.6.

So CI failure = BLOCKING per instructions. The fix would be to split parkBlockedPr into smaller functions or add tests covering the branches to lower CRAP. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)² + CC. CC=13. For CRAP ≤ 8, need coverage: 13²(1-cov)² + 13 ≤ 8 → impossible (CRAP ≥ CC = 13 > 8). So the function must be refactored to reduce complexity below 8, or the CRAP check... Since CRAP ≥ CC always, parkBlockedPr with CC 13 can never pass threshold 8. Must refactor: split into helpers (e.g., `stripArmFromPr`, `stripArmFromIssue` — each small), reducing each function's complexity.

Now the second major finding: the label-shape bug. Let me verify what `github_list_prs` returns — REST list PRs returns labels as objects. Check ghHelpers.findPRForTicket and how other code handles labels from scm.listPrs. Let me look for existing patterns of reading pr.labels from listPrs in the codebase.

Confirmed: the codebase explicitly documents that REST labels are `[{name}]` objects (see `prHasApproved` comment: "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"). The new `parkBlockedPr` uses `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` — with object labels this always returns -1. Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. Wait — is that wrong though? If the PR still has agent:rework and is unblocked, a rework leg would fire... The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the test mocks labels as plain strings, so the test is green while production behavior differs — a brittle/mock-shape test.

Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). The real bug is not normalizing `{name}` objects.

How does the live PR object actually reach handleReworkBlocked? Via requirePrForTicket → findPRForTicket → scm.listPrs('open') → github_list_prs → REST payload with labels as {name} objects. Unless the bridge normalizes. Let me check if there's normalization in scm.js or the bridge. Check `_githubListPrs` wrapper — in scm.js line 514, listPrs directly returns github_list_prs output. Is there any mapping? Look for where listPrs results get post-processed, e.g., in pullRequest.js or elsewhere. Let me check how mutexRegistry labelHoldersOf handles it — earlier comment in githubSource said "the github_list_prs carrier uses `number`" and prLabels(p) normalizes `(p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; })` at line 110. That's the SM path normalizing. The rework path doesn't.

Let me double-check the actual bridge global github_list_prs definition — maybe it's in native/ or a global bridge function that parses MCP output. Search for where it's defined for tests: js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js defines global.github_list_prs — check its shape to see convention.

So `parkBlockedPr`'s guard:
```js
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```
With production data: prLabels = [{name:'agent:rework'}], indexOf('agent:rework') = -1, length = 1 > 0 → return → skip removal. Both arms skipped. PR never stripped.

Also note: `handleReworkBlocked` is called with `pr` from `requirePrForTicket` (raw listPrs object). But wait — is there a path where labels are normalized before? The new code's `indexOf(arm)` fails, and the early-return guard prevents stripping. This is a genuine production bug (partial AC failure, silent) → BLOCKING? Let's classify: the primary AC "strips arms from both the PR and the issue" fails for the PR in production. The `blocked` label addition works, which does stop the loop (the freeze is what stops re-dispatch). But on human unblock, the stale `agent:rework` arm on the PR... does any rule dispatch rework from PR-side arm without issue status? PR-side rules (pr-rework etc.) match queries with issue carriers; the issue is at status:Blocked. The SM pr-type rules read PR labels + linked issue. If a human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR while the issue stays at status:Blocked, does the rework rule fire? The rework rule presumably requires the issue NOT in blocked status... unclear. Regardless, AC explicitly requires the strip on both carriers, the PR description claims it works, and the test gives false confidence. I'd class this BLOCKING? Another point: the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — when pr.labels is missing entirely (undefined → []), length 0 → proceeds to removeLabel best-effort. OK-ish.

Second issue: the test mocks `listPrs` returning labels as plain strings `['agent:rework','agent:review']` — doesn't match production `{name}` shape. Same class of issue.

Third: CI failure — CRAP 14.6 > 8 for new function, CC=13. CRAP ≥ CC, so must split the function. BLOCKING (red CI per formatting rules F7).

{"content":"# Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

## Summary
The fix direction is right, but two blockers: CI is red — the Quality ratchet rejects the new `parkBlockedPr` (CC 13 / CRAP 14.6 > threshold 8, and since CRAP ≥ CC no test coverage alone can bring it under) — and the PR-side arm strip silently no-ops in production because raw REST labels are `{name}` objects, so `agent:rework` stays on the PR and a human unblock would re-arm a stale rework leg (AC1 violated).

## Key Issues
- 🚨 **CI failure (Quality / crap)**: `NEW > 8 js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6` — new function over CRAP_THRESHOLD; must be split into small helpers (the file already has the gh-957 CRAP-split pattern to follow).
- 🚨 **PR arms never stripped in production**: `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` on `[{name}]` REST label objects always misses, and the `prLabels.length > 0` guard then early-returns — only the issue-side arms are actually removed.
- 💡 Test mocks PR labels as plain strings, masking the production shape; mock `{name: 'agent:rework'}` objects instead.

## Next Steps
1. Split `parkBlockedPr` into per-carrier helpers (label-block / strip-PR-arm / strip-issue-arm) so each new function stays under CC 8.
2. Normalize `pr.labels` (`l.name || l`, same as `githubSource.prLabels` / `prHasApproved`) or drop the absent-guard and best-effort `removeLabel` exactly like the issue-side loop.
3. Update the gh-1060 test to use the REST `{name}` label shape so it fails without the normalization.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Quality gate (crap) fails — `parkBlockedPr` is a new function over CRAP_THRESHOLD**

CI run 39159378802 failed at the `crap4js ratchet` step with:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`parkBlockedPr` measures CC 13. CRAP is bounded below by CC (`CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)² + CC`), so no amount of added test coverage can push a CC-13 function under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` that applies to functions not in `crap-baseline.json` — only lowering the cyclomatic complexity works.

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: mock the production REST label shape — `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]` objects, not plain strings**

```javascript
labels: [{ name: 'agent:rework' }, { name: 'agent:review' }]
```

That single change makes the gh-1060 test a true RED→GREEN guard for the label normalization, instead of only asserting the string-shape code path. `js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js` and the githubSource suites use the object shape for the same reason.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
