**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: Quality gate (crap) fails — `parkBlockedPr` is a new function over CRAP_THRESHOLD**

CI run 39159378802 failed at the `crap4js ratchet` step with:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`parkBlockedPr` measures CC 13. CRAP is bounded below by CC (`CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)² + CC`), so no amount of added test coverage can push a CC-13 function under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` that applies to functions not in `crap-baseline.json` — only lowering the cyclomatic complexity works.

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```
This is the rework round. No ci_failures.md this time (CI presumably passed or not yet run). Let me read the current diff and check whether my two blocking findings are fixed.

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });

### Root Cause

- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

```

Then the guard: `indexOf === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` → if the PR has ANY labels (length > 0, e.g. `agent:rework` as objects), it returns early — **the arms are never stripped from the PR in production**! Only `blocked` is added; agent:rework remains on the PR.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: mock the production REST label shape — `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]` objects, not plain strings**

This mock is what lets the green suite mask the production bug in `parkBlockedPr` (the PR-side strip never fires against real `{name}` label objects). Please change the mock to the real REST shape:

```javascript
labels: [{ name: 'agent:rework' }, { name: 'agent:review' }]
```

That single change makes the gh-1060 test a true RED→GREEN guard for the label normalization, instead of only asserting the string-shape code path. `js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js` and the githubSource suites use the object shape for the same reason.

- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

`parkBlockedPr` measures CC 13. CRAP is bounded below by CC (`CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)² + CC`), so no amount of added test coverage can push a CC-13 function under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` that applies to functions not in `crap-baseline.json` — only lowering the cyclomatic complexity works.

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```
This is the rework round. No ci_failures.md this time (CI presumably passed or not yet run). Let me read the current diff and check whether my two blocking findings are fixed.

My local run had all N/A coverage so the ratchet couldn't flag it — a local artifact (paths). Doesn't matter; CI truth: parkBlockedPr CC 13, CRAP 14.6.

So CI failure = BLOCKING per instructions. The fix would be to split parkBlockedPr into smaller functions or add tests covering the branches to lower CRAP. CRAP = CC²(1-cov)² + CC. CC=13. For CRAP ≤ 8, need coverage: 13²(1-cov)² + 13 ≤ 8 → impossible (CRAP ≥ CC = 13 > 8). So the function must be refactored to reduce complexity below 8, or the CRAP check... Since CRAP ≥ CC always, parkBlockedPr with CC 13 can never pass threshold 8. Must refactor: split into helpers (e.g., `stripArmFromPr`, `stripArmFromIssue` — each small), reducing each function's complexity.

Now the second major finding: the label-shape bug. Let me verify what `github_list_prs` returns — REST list PRs returns labels as objects. Check ghHelpers.findPRForTicket and how other code handles labels from scm.listPrs. Let me look for existing patterns of reading pr.labels from listPrs in the codebase.

Confirmed: the codebase explicitly documents that REST labels are `[{name}]` objects (see `prHasApproved` comment: "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"). The new `parkBlockedPr` uses `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` — with object labels this always returns -1. Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. Wait — is that wrong though? If the PR still has agent:rework and is unblocked, a rework leg would fire... The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the test mocks labels as plain strings, so the test is green while production behavior differs — a brittle/mock-shape test.

Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). The real bug is not normalizing `{name}` objects.

How does the live PR object actually reach handleReworkBlocked? Via requirePrForTicket → findPRForTicket → scm.listPrs('open') → github_list_prs → REST payload with labels as {name} objects. Unless the bridge normalizes. Let me check if there's normalization in scm.js or the bridge. Check `_githubListPrs` wrapper — in scm.js line 514, listPrs directly returns github_list_prs output. Is there any mapping? Look for where listPrs results get post-processed, e.g., in pullRequest.js or elsewhere. Let me check how mutexRegistry labelHoldersOf handles it — earlier comment in githubSource said "the github_list_prs carrier uses `number`" and prLabels(p) normalizes `(p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; })` at line 110. That's the SM path normalizing. The rework path doesn't.

Let me double-check the actual bridge global github_list_prs definition — maybe it's in native/ or a global bridge function that parses MCP output. Search for where it's defined for tests: js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js defines global.github_list_prs — check its shape to see convention.

So `parkBlockedPr`'s guard:
```js
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```
With production data: prLabels = [{name:'agent:rework'}], indexOf('agent:rework') = -1, length = 1 > 0 → return → skip removal. Both arms skipped. PR never stripped.

Also note: `handleReworkBlocked` is called with `pr` from `requirePrForTicket` (raw listPrs object). But wait — is there a path where labels are normalized before? Let's classify: the primary AC "strips arms from both the PR and the issue" fails for the PR in production. The `blocked` label addition works, which does stop the loop (the freeze is what stops re-dispatch). But on human unblock, the stale `agent:rework` arm on the PR... does any rule dispatch rework from PR-side arm without issue status? PR-side rules (pr-rework etc.) match queries with issue carriers; the issue is at status:Blocked. The SM pr-type rules read PR labels + linked issue. If a human unblocks by removing `blocked` from the PR while the issue stays at status:Blocked, does the rework rule fire? ## Summary
The fix direction is right, but two blockers: CI is red — the Quality ratchet rejects the new `parkBlockedPr` (CC 13 / CRAP 14.6 > threshold 8, and since CRAP ≥ CC no test coverage alone can bring it under) — and the PR-side arm strip silently no-ops in production because raw REST labels are `{name}` objects, so `agent:rework` stays on the PR and a human unblock would re-arm a stale rework leg (AC1 violated).

## Key Issues
- 🚨 **CI failure (Quality / crap)**: `NEW > 8 js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6` — new function over CRAP_THRESHOLD; must be split into small helpers (the file already has the gh-957 CRAP-split pattern to follow).
- 🚨 **PR arms never stripped in production**: `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` on `[{name}]` REST label objects always misses, and the `prLabels.length > 0` guard then early-returns — only the issue-side arms are actually removed.
- 💡 Test mocks PR labels as plain strings, masking the production shape; mock `{name: 'agent:rework'}` objects instead.

## Next Steps
1. Split `parkBlockedPr` into per-carrier helpers (label-block / strip-PR-arm / strip-issue-arm) so each new function stays under CC 8.
2. Normalize `pr.labels` (`l.name || l`, same as `githubSource.prLabels` / `prHasApproved`) or drop the absent-guard and best-effort `removeLabel` exactly like the issue-side loop.
3. Update the gh-1060 test to use the REST `{name}` label shape so it fails without the normalization.

Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). The real bug is not normalizing `{name}` objects.

var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });

- **Title**: gh-1060 BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +131
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T19:34:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:58:24Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: Quality gate (crap) fails — `parkBlockedPr` is a new function over CRAP_THRESHOLD**

CI run 39159378802 failed at the `crap4js ratchet` step with:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`parkBlockedPr` measures CC 13. CRAP is bounded below by CC (`CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)² + CC`), so no amount of added test coverage can push a CC-13 function under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` that applies to functions not in `crap-baseline.json` — only lowering the cyclomatic complexity works.

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```
This is the rework round. No ci_failures.md this time (CI presumably passed or not yet run). Let me read the current diff and check whether my two blocking findings are fixed.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: mock the production REST label shape — `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]` objects, not plain strings**

### Root Cause

- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage

- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.

```javascript

```

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: mock the production REST label shape — `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]` objects, not plain strings**

This mock is what lets the green suite mask the production bug in `parkBlockedPr` (the PR-side strip never fires against real `{name}` label objects). Please change the mock to the real REST shape:

```javascript
labels: [{ name: 'agent:rework' }, { name: 'agent:review' }]
```

That single change makes the gh-1060 test a true RED→GREEN guard for the label normalization, instead of only asserting the string-shape code path. `js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js` and the githubSource suites use the object shape for the same reason.

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. - Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: mock the production REST label shape — `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]` objects, not plain strings**

This mock is what lets the green suite mask the production bug in `parkBlockedPr` (the PR-side strip never fires against real `{name}` label objects). Please change the mock to the real REST shape:

```javascript
labels: [{ name: 'agent:rework' }, { name: 'agent:review' }]
```

That single change makes the gh-1060 test a true RED→GREEN guard for the label normalization, instead of only asserting the string-shape code path. `js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js` and the githubSource suites use the object shape for the same reason.

- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`
- **State**: open

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

The new unit test mocks `labels: ['agent:rework', 'agent:review']` as plain strings, which is why the suite is green while production behavior differs — see the companion comment on the test mock.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: mock the production REST label shape — `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]` objects, not plain strings**

This mock is what lets the green suite mask the production bug in `parkBlockedPr` (the PR-side strip never fires against real `{name}` label objects). Please change the mock to the real REST shape:

```javascript
labels: [{ name: 'agent:rework' }, { name: 'agent:review' }]
```

That single change makes the gh-1060 test a true RED→GREEN guard for the label normalization, instead of only asserting the string-shape code path. `js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js` and the githubSource suites use the object shape for the same reason.

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).

- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. - Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).

Confirmed: the codebase explicitly documents that REST labels are `[{name}]` objects (see `prHasApproved` comment: "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"). The new `parkBlockedPr` uses `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` — with object labels this always returns -1. Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. Wait — is that wrong though? If the PR still has agent:rework and is unblocked, a rework leg would fire... The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the test mocks labels as plain strings, so the test is green while production behavior differs — a brittle/mock-shape test.

Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). The real bug is not normalizing `{name}` objects.

How does the live PR object actually reach handleReworkBlocked? Via requirePrForTicket → findPRForTicket → scm.listPrs('open') → github_list_prs → REST payload with labels as {name} objects. Unless the bridge normalizes. Let me check if there's normalization in scm.js or the bridge. Check `_githubListPrs` wrapper — in scm.js line 514, listPrs directly returns github_list_prs output. Is there any mapping? Look for where listPrs results get post-processed, e.g., in pullRequest.js or elsewhere. Let me check how mutexRegistry labelHoldersOf handles it — earlier comment in githubSource said "the github_list_prs carrier uses `number`" and prLabels(p) normalizes `(p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; })` at line 110. That's the SM path normalizing. The rework path doesn't.

Let me double-check the actual bridge global github_list_prs definition — maybe it's in native/ or a global bridge function that parses MCP output. Search for where it's defined for tests: js/test/bug_done_and_test_pr_merge.test.js defines global.github_list_prs — check its shape to see convention.

Confirmed. The SM layer (`githubSource.prLabels`) explicitly normalizes `{name}` objects → strings for exactly this reason. The rework path receives the raw REST payload where `pr.labels` is `[{name: 'agent:rework'}]`.

So `parkBlockedPr`'s guard:
```js
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });

- **Title**: gh-1060 BLOCKED conclusion must park the PR too: status:Blocked is set on the issue but no SM rule reads it — armed PRs loop rework legs forever (live: dart #420)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1060` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +131
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T19:34:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:58:24Z

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: Quality gate (crap) fails — `parkBlockedPr` is a new function over CRAP_THRESHOLD**

CI run 39159378802 failed at the `crap4js ratchet` step with:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/pushReworkChanges.js::parkBlockedPr: 14.6
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`parkBlockedPr` measures CC 13. CRAP is bounded below by CC (`CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)² + CC`), so no amount of added test coverage can push a CC-13 function under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` that applies to functions not in `crap-baseline.json` — only lowering the cyclomatic complexity works.

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```
This is the rework round. No ci_failures.md this time (CI presumably passed or not yet run). Let me read the current diff and check whether my two blocking findings are fixed.

blocks.text:
Confirmed: the codebase explicitly documents that REST labels are `[{name}]` objects (see `prHasApproved` comment: "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"). The new `parkBlockedPr` uses `prLabels.indexOf(arm)` — with object labels this always returns -1. Then the guard `prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0 → return` fires whenever the PR carries ANY label (length > 0) — which a rework PR always does (`agent:rework` itself!). So in production:

- PR has labels `[{name:'agent:rework'}]` → length 1 > 0, indexOf returns -1 → early return → **agent:rework and agent:review are NEVER stripped from the PR**.
- The `blocked` label IS added (that part works).
- Issue-side arms ARE stripped (tracker path has no guard).

Partial result: PR is frozen by `blocked` (good — the SM freeze works, the loop stops), but the PR keeps its `agent:rework` arm. Consequence on unblock: "stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — FAILS for the PR side; the moment a human removes `blocked`, the armed PR re-dispatches a rework leg. Wait — is that wrong though? If the PR still has agent:rework and is unblocked, a rework leg would fire... The ticket is at status:Blocked on the issue; does any rule dispatch rework based on the PR arm alone? The rework rules match on issue status + PR labels presumably. The AC says "strips agent:rework / agent:review arms from both the PR and the issue — one atomic park". So this is a partial AC violation: the PR-side strip silently no-ops in production. Also the test mocks labels as plain strings, so the test is green while production behavior differs — a brittle/mock-shape test.

Also the guard logic itself is confused: `indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0` — "absent — nothing to strip" — but if labels array is EMPTY (length 0), it proceeds to call removeLabel. That inverts intent: when labels are unknown/empty it calls removeLabel anyway (best-effort OK), but when labels are known and arm absent... fine. The `prLabels.length > 0` condition seems designed to distinguish "labels not fetched" from "fetched and empty" — but an actually-empty label list would also trigger removeLabel, causing a harmless 404 (caught). ## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```

if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });

## PR Description

Closes #1060
### Root Cause
- A rework leg concluding BLOCKED (agents#827 contract) only set the issue's `status:Blocked` — no SM rule reads that label, so the PR kept its `agent:rework` arm and every tick re-dispatched a rework leg on the blocked ticket (live: dart gh-395 / PR #420, run 39156398849, 2026-10-18 18:55Z).
- Two parallel "blocked" vocabularies with no bridge: the SM's park vocabulary is the PR-side `blocked` label (engine-level freeze in `githubSource`), which the blocked post-action never wrote.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` — new `parkBlockedPr()` called from `handleReworkBlocked`: one atomic park — labels the PR `blocked` (scm.addLabel) and strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` from BOTH the PR (scm.removeLabel) and the issue (tracker.removeLabel), next to the existing Blocked move. All writes best-effort so a label-write failure never masks the Blocked move. Blocked PR comment updated to describe the park.
- Dev leg: no change needed — `completeBlockedPath` (developBugAndCreatePR) runs after Path 0, which returns early whenever an open PR exists, so at blocked-conclusion time there is no linked PR to park by construction.

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `test_pushReworkChanges.js` — new gh-1060 test in the agents#827 suite: simulated blocked conclusion asserts PR carries `blocked`, arms stripped from both carriers. Failed before the fix, passes after.
- AC3 (next tick dispatches nothing): engine-level freeze already covered by `test_smGithubSource.js` (blocked PRs invisible to every rule incl. issue-carriers; mutex transparency).
- AC2 (symmetric unblock): covered by existing test "removing the label re-exposes the item unchanged" — no SM rule reads `status:Blocked`, so there is no hidden second switch; no auto-unblock heuristic added (non-goal).
- Full suite: 4336 passed, 0 failed (164 files via node_testRunner).

The codebase already has the established pattern for exactly this: see the `gh-957 CRAP split` comment right below (`handleReworkBlocked` area) — extract small single-responsibility helpers, each covered by the suite so the ratchet stays under threshold. For example:

- `labelPrBlocked(scm, pr)` — the addLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromPr(scm, pr, arm)` — the per-arm removeLabel try/catch
- `stripArmFromIssue(tracker, ticketKey, arm)` — the tracker-side loop

Each of those is ~CC 3–4. This also fixes the second blocker (label-shape guard) at the same time, since the strip helper is where the normalization belongs.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: PR-side arms are never stripped in production — `indexOf` against REST `{name}` label objects always misses, then the guard early-returns**

The `pr` object here comes from `requirePrForTicket` → `findPRForTicket` → `scm.listPrs('open')`, i.e. the raw GitHub REST list payload, where labels are **`[{name: 'agent:rework'}, …]` objects, not strings**. The codebase documents and handles this everywhere it touches raw PR labels:

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:110` — `prLabels(p)` maps `(l && l.name) || l` for exactly this reason
- `prHasApproved` (this file, ~line 131) — "REST labels: [{name}] objects or strings"
- `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent` (`js/common/pullRequest.js:191`) — same normalization

With production data, `prLabels.indexOf('agent:rework')` returns `-1`, and since a rework PR always carries at least one label (`agent:rework` itself → `prLabels.length > 0`), this line early-returns for **both** arms:

```javascript
if (prLabels.indexOf(arm) === -1 && prLabels.length > 0) return; // absent — nothing to strip
```

Result: AC1's "strips `agent:rework` / `agent:review` arms from **both** the PR and the issue" silently degrades to issue-only. The `blocked` label add does freeze the pair (the loop stops), but the PR keeps its stale arm — precisely the state the PR description warns about ("stripped arms mean no stale arm fires on re-admission" — false for the PR side).

Note the issue-side loop below has no such guard at all — it just best-effort `removeLabel`s. The simplest correct fix is to drop the guard and do the same on the PR side (a 404 on an absent label is already tolerated by the try/catch), or normalize first:

```javascript
var names = (pr.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
```
